name: RTP descent geo pack: satellite plates, terrain and labels

frame.name: rtp_local
frame.three: three (x, y, z) = rtp_local (x, height, -y); north is -z. Same frame as twin/web/models/exterior (not recentred).
frame.note: Every plate is resampled so this linear conversion is exact for it (rows evenly spaced in latitude, columns in longitude). The flat frame's east-west scale is exact at the pin's latitude and off by 0.14% at the 50 km plate's north and south edges, 0.6% at the 200 km plate's and up to 2.4% at the 800 km backdrop's (the same frame the twin uses, so nothing drifts against it).

The *_2026 plates: Copernicus Sentinel-2 data, free and open for any use including commercial (Sentinel Data Legal Notice, linked in each plate's source.licence); the notice 'Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2026' must be shown.
imagery_dates: The EOX plates are a 2016 mosaic: they show the ground as it was in 2016. Anything built since (for example the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link across the harbour south of Vashi, opened in 2024) is not in them, while the 3D context buildings come from Overture 2026. Do not label anything that only exists after 2016 on those plates.
SCRIPT.md (B01-B04 notes) quotes 'Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2026'. That is only true where the *_2026 plates are on screen; on the EOX plates it must read 2016.

The *_2026 plates (50 km, flight corridor, 12 km, 6.4 km) come from one cloud-free satellite pass of 12 Nov 2026 (two adjoining Sentinel-2 tiles of the same pass), so they match today's ground and the Overture buildings, and they are visibly sharper than the EOX mosaic at these scales. Use them from the 50 km plate down; the 800 km and 200 km plates stay 2016, where change is invisible from that height.

grade.note: One fixed grade for every plate (a levels stretch, since the source is flat; slight desaturation; a gentle S-curve; warm shadows and highlights; a light matte lift), so plates never shift colour during a crossfade. Ungraded copies are in raw/.

edits: Open sea (800 km and 200 km plates only): beyond the imaged coastal water EOX shows a flat navy (24, 44, 77) with a hard edge. The graded plates fade the coastal water's own colour out into that navy over 3 % of the plate width (24 km and 6 km), on the navy side only. Nothing on land or in the imaged water is changed. The raw/ copies keep the original edge.

Known blemishes in the source, all at the far edges of the 800 km plate and hidden by an edge fade: a lighter rectangle over the Gulf of Kutch (top-left corner) and a straight scene seam in the Gulf of Khambhat.

terrain.layout: row-major, cols x rows values; row 0 = north edge, last row = south edge; columns west to east; the first and last vertices sit exactly on the mosaic's edges. Same vertex order as THREE.PlaneGeometry(width, height, cols-1, rows-1) after rotateX(-Math.PI/2) (then moved to the mosaic's three_plane.center): set position.y of vertex k to heights[k] * exaggeration.
terrain.heights: metres above the site ground (the twin's y = 0, 11.557 m above sea level); the sea is at sea_level_m
terrain.ground_model: Copernicus DSM with buildings and trees removed (150 m minimum filter, smoothed), hills kept; the twin's recipe with a smooth instead of a hard hill switch. Agrees with the twin's own terrain (exterior/tools/prep_data.py) to a median 0.2 m inside +-3 km (0.8 m at most inside 560 m; up to about 15 m on the steepest hill flanks, where the twin's sampling window sits a third of a cell off the source grid).
terrain.smoothing: 13 x 13 source cells averaged before sampling
terrain.exaggeration_note: Plates overlap, so use one factor for every plate on screen; otherwise the coarser plate's hills poke through the finer one. 1.0 is true scale; up to 1.5 reads well from above 20 km.

how_to_use: Descent order: west_coast_800km -> mumbai_region_200km -> mumbai_navi_mumbai_50km -> flight_corridor -> airoli_12km -> rtp_6400m -> the 3D twin. All plates but flight_corridor are squares centred on the pin; flight_corridor is the 28 x 22 km rectangle SCRIPT.md asks for, off-centre (see its three_plane.center). Stack them coarse to fine. Give finer plates a higher renderOrder (or a small polygonOffset) rather than separating them in height, and fade each plate's outer 8-10 % to transparent in the shader so no edge ever shows.

Vintage: from the 50 km plate down, use the *_2026 files (mosaics_2026: same ground, same bounds, same terrain grids, matched colour). They show today's ground under the 2026 buildings and are much sharper. Keep the 2016 files only as a fallback.

Crossfade by camera altitude. suggested_full_frame_altitude_m is the height at which the plate just fills a 16:9 screen with a 45 degree vertical field of view looking straight down; fade the next finer plate in from about 1.5x its own figure down to its figure.

Terrain: build PlaneGeometry(width, height, cols-1, rows-1), rotateX(-Math.PI/2), move it to three_plane.center, then set each vertex's y from the .f32 file (fetch -> arrayBuffer -> new Float32Array). Use the same mosaic as its texture. Heights are already relative to the site ground, matching the twin.

The twin's own rtp_terrain.glb covers the 6.4 km square of the rtp_6400m plate and is flattened inside 560 m; when the twin is on screen, fade out the coarser plates near the centre or drop them 1-2 m so they never cut through it.
Sentinel-2 detail stops at 10 m per pixel, so below roughly 1.5 km camera height hand over to the 3D context model.

rtp_6400m drapes straight onto twin/web/models/exterior/rtp_terrain.glb (the same 6.4 km square): uv = ((x + 3200) / 6400, (y + 3200) / 6400) with y north, i.e. u = (three.x + 3200) / 6400, v = (3200 - three.z) / 6400, texture.flipY left at true.
Water level: the sea and Thane Creek sit at sea_level_m (-11.557 m in the twin's frame). A water plane there, with a little sky reflection, makes the creek read as water when the camera tilts.
Earth's curve (optional, for very high shots): lower each vertex by d * d / 12742000 m, where d is its distance from the pin in metres (about 785 m at 100 km).

Labels: x_m, y_m are rtp_local metres; three = [x, 0, -y]. Thane Creek also carries path_m, the OSM line, for a label that follows the water. straight_line_km_from_pin is a straight line computed from the coordinates, not a travel distance.
